title: the breath again — every claim checked
hook: a son keeps bringing his father an answer, and the father keeps sending him back, past food, past breath
carry: the breath again — every claim checked

segments.voice: Yesterday, the breath again: in the Gita, some offer the in-breath into the out-breath, one gift in a row of gifts. Did one breath get set down as a gift? Day one thousand three hundred twenty-seven.

Breath is Brahman. That's the second answer a young man named Bhrigu brings home to his father, Varuna, in the third part of the Taittiriya Upanishad. We met him over food, his first answer. The clue hasn't changed: Brahman is that from which beings are born, by which they live, and into which they return. Go and practice, and find out. Food fit the clue, and still he was sent out again. Now he's back with breath. On the last day of a season built on checking claims: the step after food, and what the Upanishad says breath is.
screen: `BREATH IS BRAHMAN.` → `THE SECOND ANSWER.` → `ONE HONEST ANSWER AT A TIME.`

segments.voice: Here's how the second answer comes, in paraphrase. Bhrigu practices again, and comes to see that breath is Brahman. From breath beings are born, by breath they live, into breath they return. It fits the clue. The second part of the same Upanishad has a short verse that says why. In paraphrase: the gods breathe along with breath, and so do people, and so do animals. Breath is the life of beings, so it's called the life of all. Look at what kind of claim that is. It names no technique. It promises no cure. It points at something plain enough to check against your own body: while there's life, there's breath. That's a claim that grew when we checked it. And still Varuna says, practice again. Bhrigu goes on, to mind, to understanding, and at last to bliss, and this time he isn't sent away. That's a fitting shape for closing this season on Ayurveda as a lens. The doshas as a way of noticing, not a diagnosis. The day's rhythm, the seasons, food, sleep, and these last days, breath, with every claim given a label: the text says, tradition says, a doctor decides. Breath as the power the senses follow, like bees. Breath as a king sending out officers. Breath resting on a steady seat. Breath tamed slowly, like a lion. Breath given as an offering. Some claims grew when we checked them, and some shrank. Bhrigu's way sits under all of it. Bring an answer. Test it against the clue. Keep what holds, and stay willing to be sent out again.
screen: `BREATH IS BRAHMAN` · `BREATH IS THE LIFE OF BEINGS` · `MIND, UNDERSTANDING, THEN BLISS` · `KEEP WHAT HOLDS, LOOK FURTHER`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: climb Bhrigu's steps, slowly. Sit comfortably. First, notice the body, the food that built it, the weight on the seat. Then notice the breath, coming and going on its own. Then notice the mind, thoughts arriving and leaving. Then notice the knowing, the part that is aware of all of it. Then simply rest, and let whatever ease is there be enough. Nothing to reach. If you pray, you can rest in God's presence. The bell holds the time.
The breath again. In the Taittiriya, Bhrigu finds that breath is Brahman, and his father sends him on, past breath, to look further. Today's word.

Your line: the breath again — every claim checked. Today, take one answer you're sure of and practice again: test it, keep what holds. Tomorrow, a new season, the women of the epics, starting with Sita. Day one thousand three hundred twenty-seven.

howItsDone: The Taittiriya Upanishad's story of Bhrigu is studied in Vedanta as a teaching on the layers of a person, food, breath, mind, understanding and bliss, and is also chanted in Vedic recitation.

myth: in the Taittiriya, gods, people and animals breathe along with breath
breath is the life of beings, the verse says, so it's called the life of all.
in the Taittiriya, beings are born from breath, live by it and return into it
breath fits the father's clue, and it's one true step on the way.
the Taittiriya's verse on breath teaches a breathing technique
it names no technique and promises no cure. it points at breath as the life of beings.

fork.setup: the Taittiriya says gods, people and animals all breathe along with breath. what does it go on to call breath?
options: a secret energy for the few.
the life of beings, the life of all.
the body's fuel, and nothing more.
fork.reveal: breath is the life of beings, the verse says, so it's called the life of all. no technique, no cure, and Bhrigu still goes further, to mind, understanding and bliss.

original.note: Sanskrit: bliss, joy. in the Taittiriya, the last step of Bhrigu's search, after food, breath, mind and understanding.

trapdoor: what you thought: an old text about breath must be selling a technique.
what it means: the Taittiriya calls breath the life of beings, and Bhrigu finds it a true step on the way to bliss.
what a scholar hears: prano hi bhutanam ayuh in Taittiriya 2.3, beside Bhrigu's breath step in 3.3, on the ladder anna, prana, manas, vijnana, ananda.
recall: a warrior, and a daughter coming home
